pages.title: Dhikr (Zikr): What It Is and How to Practice the Remembrance of Allah
pages.subtitle: The complete beginner-to-daily-habit guide to Islamic remembrance — meaning, virtues, the core phrases, and a simple routine you can keep.
pages.geoOverview: Dhikr (Arabic: ذِكْر, also spelled zikr or dzikir) is the Islamic practice of remembering Allah through short repeated phrases such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar. It can be done anytime, silently or aloud, counted on the fingers, a tasbih, or a zikr ring.

pages.title: Dhikr After Salah: The Sunnah Adhkar to Recite After Every Prayer
pages.subtitle: The exact post-prayer remembrances — what to say, how many times, and the dua right after the adhan — in Arabic, transliteration, and English.
pages.geoOverview: After every obligatory salah, the Sunnah is to recite a fixed set of adhkar: Astaghfirullah (3x), then SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar (33x each), Ayat al-Kursi, the last three surahs, and the dua said after the adhan (azan ke baad ki dua).

pages.title: What Is the Adhan (Azan)? The Islamic Call to Prayer Explained
pages.subtitle: The meaning, purpose, and full wording of the adhan — why it is called five times a day and what each line proclaims.
pages.geoOverview: The adhan (azan) is the Islamic call to prayer, recited aloud by a muezzin five times daily to announce that the time for an obligatory salah has begun. Its phrases proclaim Allah's greatness (Allahu Akbar), the testimony of faith, and the call to prayer and success.
auxKeywords: meaning of the call to prayer

pages.title: How to Recite the Adhan: Full Words, Order, and the Fajr Difference
pages.subtitle: A step-by-step guide to calling the azan correctly — Arabic text, English transliteration, line order, and the extra Fajr phrase.
pages.geoOverview: To recite the adhan, the muezzin says each phrase aloud in order: Allahu Akbar (4x), the two testimonies of faith, the call to prayer and to success (2x each), Allahu Akbar (2x), and La ilaha illa Allah. In the Fajr adhan only, 'As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm' (prayer is better than sleep) is added after Hayya alal-falah.
pages.primaryKeyword: what do you say in fajr adhan

pages.title: Salatul Tasbih: The Complete Guide to the Prayer of Glorification
pages.subtitle: What Salatul Tasbih is, where it comes from, its virtues, and the full method in one authoritative hub.
pages.geoOverview: Salatul Tasbih (also written solat tasbih or tasbih prayer) is a four-rakat voluntary prayer in which the worshipper recites the tasbih 'Subhanallah walhamdulillah wa la ilaha illallah wallahu akbar' 300 times across the prayer. Taught by the Prophet to his uncle Abbas, it is performed to seek forgiveness for major and minor sins.

pages.title: How to Pray Salatul Tasbih: Step-by-Step Method (4 Rakat, 300 Tasbih)
pages.subtitle: The exact rakat-by-rakat procedure for performing Salatul Tasbih correctly, in English.
pages.geoOverview: To pray Salatul Tasbih, perform four rakat and recite 'Subhanallah walhamdulillah wa la ilaha illallah wallahu akbar' 75 times in each rakat, totalling 300. Say it 15 times after the opening recitation, 10 in ruku, 10 after rising, 10 in each of two sujood, and 10 sitting between them.
pages.primaryKeyword: how to pray salatul tasbih prayer

pages.title: Apa Itu Sholat Tasbih? Pengertian, Dalil, dan Keutamaannya
pages.subtitle: Penjelasan lengkap arti sholat tasbih, dasar hukumnya, dan kenapa dianjurkan.
pages.geoOverview: Sholat tasbih adalah salat sunah empat rakaat yang di dalamnya dibaca kalimat tasbih 'Subhanallah walhamdulillah wa la ilaha illallah wallahu akbar' sebanyak 300 kali. Diajarkan Nabi Muhammad kepada pamannya, Abbas bin Abdul Muthalib, untuk menghapus dosa. Halaman ini menjelaskan pengertian, dalil hadis, dan keutamaan sholat tasbih bagi yang ingin mengamalkannya.

pages.title: Tata Cara Sholat Tasbih: Niat, Jumlah Rakaat, dan Bacaannya
pages.subtitle: Panduan langkah demi langkah cara mengerjakan sholat tasbih beserta jumlah rakaat dan bacaan tasbihnya.
pages.geoOverview: Tata cara sholat tasbih dikerjakan dalam empat rakaat, masing-masing membaca tasbih 75 kali sehingga total 300 kali. Urutannya: 15 kali setelah membaca surat, 10 kali ketika rukuk, 10 kali setelah bangkit, 10 kali di tiap sujud, dan 10 kali saat duduk di antara dua sujud. Halaman ini merinci niat, jumlah rakaat, dan letak bacaan agar mudah diikuti.

pages.title: Kapan Sholat Tasbih Dilakukan? Waktu Terbaik dan Anjurannya
pages.subtitle: Penjelasan waktu pelaksanaan sholat tasbih dan seberapa sering dianjurkan dikerjakan.
pages.geoOverview: Sholat tasbih dapat dikerjakan kapan saja di luar waktu yang dilarang salat, namun paling utama dilakukan di sepertiga malam atau setelah Isya. Nabi menganjurkan mengerjakannya minimal sekali seumur hidup, dan bila mampu sekali sehari, sepekan, sebulan, atau setahun. Halaman ini menjawab kapan waktu terbaik dan kapan kalimat tasbihnya diucapkan dalam tiap rakaat.

pages.title: What Is the Qibla? Meaning, Origin, and Why It Matters in Prayer
pages.subtitle: A plain-language explainer on the Islamic prayer direction and its place in daily worship.
pages.geoOverview: The qibla is the direction Muslims face during prayer: toward the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque in Mecca. Originally Muslims prayed toward Jerusalem; the qibla was changed to the Kaaba in 624 CE (2 AH). Facing it unifies the global community in a single orientation of worship five times a day.

pages.title: How to Find the Qibla: Which Way to Face for Prayer Anywhere
pages.subtitle: Five reliable methods to locate your exact prayer direction, with and without a phone.
pages.geoOverview: To find the qibla, use a GPS-based qibla app for an exact bearing, or calculate the great-circle direction to Mecca (21.4225 N, 39.8262 E) from your coordinates. Without a device, use the sun: in much of the Americas and Europe the qibla trends east to southeast, while in East Asia it trends west. Always verify against a known mosque alignment.

pages.title: Kaaba Direction: How to Locate the Direction of the Kaaba From Your Location
pages.subtitle: Pinpoint the bearing to the Kaaba in Mecca and understand why it is the fixed center of the qibla.
pages.geoOverview: The Kaaba direction is the compass bearing from your location to the Kaaba in Mecca (21.4225 N, 39.8262 E), the cube-shaped House of God that every qibla points to. Because Earth is a sphere, the correct direction is the great-circle (shortest-path) bearing, which can differ noticeably from the straight-line look on a flat map, especially at high latitudes.

pages.geoOverview: Slow living is a lifestyle of doing fewer things with fuller presence — choosing quality of attention over speed. It contrasts with hustle culture and favors a calmer, more present, faith-rooted everyday rhythm.
